faq.q: Where does the water in a dehumidifier come from?
faq.a: It comes from the invisible water vapour in the air. When the air is cooled on the cold coil, the vapour condenses into liquid water and drips into the tank.
The dew point is the temperature at which air becomes saturated, so if it cools any further, water vapour condenses into droplets. Damp air has a higher dew point.

faq.q: Why does a dehumidifier blow out warm air?
faq.a: It is a heat pump. The heat taken from the air on the cold coil, plus the heat from the compressor, is released on the warm coil, so the air leaves slightly warmer.
asks: Does a dehumidifier heat the room?

faq.a: Cooking, showers, drying clothes and even breathing add water to the air. If it cannot escape, it condenses on cold walls and windows.

faq.q: Are there dehumidifiers without a cold coil?
faq.a: Yes. Desiccant dehumidifiers use a wheel of moisture-absorbing material and a heater instead. They work better in cold rooms such as garages.

facts: A compressor dehumidifier works by cooling air below its dew point so water vapour condenses on a cold coil.
Air leaving a compressor dehumidifier is slightly warmer than the air that went in.
